steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: How long do you plan on sitting there?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: He already knows of this place. He will turn up sooner or later.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And what will you do once he turns up?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Kill him.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Murdering a foreign dignitary is a serious crime, you know.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: We shall see.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Why do you go so far for Kjerag's sake, when you're not from Kjerag yourself?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Is it still considered 'for Kjerag's sake' if it's Enciodes's ambition?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Who can deny that up till now, despite him having his own lofty goals, that there is a part of them that is 'for Kjerag's sake'?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That sort of praise is probably what he would least like to hear.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You still haven't answered my question, you know.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: When Enciodes once mentioned to me that perhaps Kjeragandr truly existed, I thought to myself that maybe one day, I could fight those so-called 'gods' with my own two hands.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Now I see that was simply wishful thinking.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And why is that?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Enciodes had already dropped that particular plan, for one.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If he had stuck to it, do you think that you could face down a goddess who just might really exist?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Perhaps?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Here, I can only find that sort of excitement during avalanches. If I ever had the opportunity, I would definitely give it a try.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Do you think you will win?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: No. I have stood against the avalanche, but I have never once triumphed.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I understand. You are simply in it for the challenge.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And you consider the matters that are happening in this land to be suitable for that purpose.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's hardly as lofty as you think. This is just who I have grown to be, nothing more.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Very well said.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You may head back now, Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You will not find your battlefield here.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If that is what the Saintess wills, then forgive me for being unable to comply.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I will decide my own battlefield.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And what if I said that is what Kjeragandr wills?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I will then wonder, why are you the one conveying Kjeragandr's will?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I am the Saintess's maid, after all.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: So what you are saying is that the will of the Saintess is the will of Kjeragandr?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Rather, that Kjeragandr supports the Great Saintess's opinion on the matter.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: At least, that is my guess.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The Black Knight is no fool. Rather than searching all over for me, she will instead be watching over here.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She knows that I will return, and return I must.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: *sigh* If only I could return home alive.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: If I had only guessed that this place would be the center of my worries—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No, how could I have guessed? How could anyone have thought that Enciodes had the brass courage to use an entire nation's faith as a pretense for his own schemes?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: He truly is someone that the Duke was wise to invest in.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And that Saintess. Is she really not aware of a single matter going on behind the scenes?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And Degenbrecher?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She couldn't possibly be quite so single-minded as to have missed the forest for the tree.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: This is... a rock?
Why have you come, traveler from afar?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I am but a man of steadfast faith, here to admire Her visage.
She tires, and wishes to rest for today.
Come back tomorrow.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I had heard that Kjeragandr welcomes believers from afar. Do you mean to say that this is no longer the case?
The pious need not prove themselves, while the insincere need not waste their words.
You are not to take a step further today, says She.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: And if I insist?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Wha—

The Trilby Asher looks all about him. The main path by Lake Silberneherze is bustling with activity most days, and today is no exception, which is why it causes no small amount of turned heads when he suddenly appears out of nowhere.
Suddenly, he smacked himself in the face hard.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Hey, when did that guy pop up there?

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: Look, he's slapping himself for some reason.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Think he's some kinda lunatic?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Haha.

The Trilby Asher takes no note of the people around him, simply turning his body in the direction of the statue of Kjeragandr. In imitation of those devout followers, he performs a quick gesture of prayer.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Kjeragandr's blessings be upon you.
This was the first time he had done such an act since stepping into this land.
After doing so, he turns to leave without a moment's hesitation.
He had not yet noticed that, from not too far away, there was a pair of eyes watching his every move.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Degenbrecher isn't a very talkative woman, so she probably won't tell Enya about this, would she?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I don't think I went too far either, did I?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: *sigh* I've said this before, but staying a spectator is harder than it looks.
She sighs once more then turns, looking every bit like a woman grumbling about the troublesome requests of her younger sister, before blending into the throng of people like she was never there.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: Stop right there.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Ah, hello, captain.

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: Who're you?

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Well, it's like this, see. There's going to be a banquet held by Lake Silberneherze tonight, right?

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: I'm here to deliver the wine.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: Wine?

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: I had heard the news about that earlier.

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: Come with me, I'll need to verify this.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Alright, sure.

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: Stand over here. Don't move. Pat him down.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Boys, I'm just trying to drop off some drinks. Do we really need to do this whole song and dance?

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: These are special circumstances. I appreciate your cooperation.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: If you really are who you are, we will offer our deepest apologies later.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Ah, I'm afraid that you two won't have the chance to do that.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: Wha—
The vintner presses down on a device hanging at his waist, and the security cameras in the room began to rotate wildly as if possessed.

steps.name: Tschäggättä A
steps.text: Guh...

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: There's an ene—

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Nice try.

steps.name: Tschäggättä B
steps.text: Ghaah—
After the two Tschäggättä fall over, the vintner swiftly begins to operate the terminal.
As he meddles with the terminal, the cameras in the corners of the room briefly halt, before returning to their normal activity.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: From my earlier investigations, I knew that Kjerag managed to get a previous-gen OS, but it's got two fatal flaws.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: I recommend you upgrade to the latest generation when you can.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Naturally, if Kjerag were to become a part of Victoria, we would provide one free of charge.
The vintner breathes a sigh of relief, but then immediately doubles over.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Hfff— Looks like my wounds are about to reopen.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: The destructive power of the Black Knight is no joke.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: But she can hardly be everywhere all at once.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: As for Kjeragandr...

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: I'll worry about that later. At least She didn't prevent me finding this place.
He stands up again, ambling towards the nearby barrel of wine.
The barrel is heavy, but as he draws close, it is immediately obvious that there is a distinct lack of the scent of wine in the air.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: ...Haha.
What was stored inside the barrel was not wine, but metal.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: I had investigated the amount of metal Kjerag was procuring, and at the time nobody had any issue with the numbers.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: But if, say, the metal that was to be used in the construction of the statue, was not all put towards that purpose...

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Where, then, did all that remaining metal go?

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: And where is this metal in the barrels slated to go next?

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Haha, I said that while the Black Knight's fearsome, she's not so strong as to cut through steel like butter. And I was right.
He turns back to operate the terminal once more.
As his fingers unceasingly type away at the keyboard, various charts and diagrams continuously pop up on the screen above him.
After a long, long while, he finally stands up.

steps.name: Vintner?
steps.text: Anyways...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: There's still a few hours to go to the banquet—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: So allow me to give a quick inspection, Enciodes.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Are you really so much a fool that you would dare to stand against Victoria?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: So let me get this straight. You saw your father, and then you gave him a kick?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Yep, felt real good!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I wasn't that angry to begin with. But once I saw that he looked like what I assumed my papa would look like, I had the sudden urge to give him a real big kick.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, atta girl!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Speaking of which, I had the pleasure of meeting Patriarch Arctosz once when I had just arrived to Kjerag, but I haven't seen him since.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If I had remembered how he had looked, you wouldn't have had to wander around willy-nilly to find him.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, are you trying to say that I actually do look a lot like him?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm, well now that I think about it more, thanks to that beard of his... Even if I had been drinking with him yesterday, I don't think it would have been that easy to notice.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I told him already, that bearded look just isn't in these days.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What if... he shaved it off?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, nothing. Don't mind me.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, look over there! That's a whole lotta burdenbeasts.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, the villagers from nearby are here too.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm thinking that this will be a mighty fine night.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: There's a burdenbeast bumping its head against you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: If it isn't my lovely Lily!

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Haha, that girl ran over the moment she spotted you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Good girl, good girl.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hey, dedushka, this is the Lily you were talking about?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Indeed. She was the first burdenbeast I met when I arrived in Kjerag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And she has become, dare I say, my dearest friend ever since I arrived.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, aren't you a little cutie-pie!

steps.name: Lily
steps.text: (Rough braying)

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Ooo, can I pet her?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But of course. Lily's an affectionate girl.

steps.name: Lily
steps.text: (Affectionate humming)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I think she likes you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha! Rosalind, it seems you really do have Kjerag blood in you!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Whoa! She's licking me!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Do you want to ride her?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Can I?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It should be alright, right, Leones?

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Hahaha, it's alright, kid.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Alright! Help me up a bit, dedushka!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Okay, grab on to my hand, and a one, two, three—!

steps.name: Lily
steps.text: (Excited rumbling)

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Wow, Lily's real steady!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I think I'll go on a stroll with her!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Go on ahead, now.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Heh, she sure is a lively little kid, now, isn't she?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You don't need to tell me. My daughter was the same at her age.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Here, for you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This is—

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Some of our best cheese. Just finished ripening today.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: I remembered that you were going back home pretty soon, so I whipped up this block just for you. I'd hoped I would see you tonight, so I brought it along just in case.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I appreciate the gesture, but are you sure it's alright? Doesn't your family need this cheese to sell?

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Oh, think nothing of it. You've helped my family and our burdenbeasts plenty.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: I'd say that I owe you for medical expenses.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: So here, consider this cheese your veterinary fee.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, alright, if you insist.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Couldn't ask for a better parting gift, if you ask me.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Truth be told, when you first showed up, we were pretty wary of you.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: But after a whole month with you, I feel like we're the best of friends.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: So I'm not going to get too mushy with you. Just remember that the next time you're in Kjerag, we'll always have space at the table for you at my farm.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I will. I really will.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Ah, Leone, are you acquainted with the Lord Viscount as well?

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Ah, Saintess! Yes, Harold here's become a right celebrity here in our little village.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I see. I hope that you and your burdenbeasts continue to enjoy yourselves.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Oh, please, getting to meet the Saintess is plenty of joy for me already!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: This banquet sure is festive, Holy Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Though there will be plenty of pomp and circumstance at the ceremony tomorrow, the populace at large will only be able to watch it via the news cameras.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Which is why I arranged for this banquet, to allow all of Kjerag to enjoy the holiday cheer.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You truly are a great Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: May I ask where the Trilby Asher might be?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: He's a bit of a somber fellow, not a great lover of festivities.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I would hardly say that, My Lord.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: While it's true that I'm not a fan of festive crowds, that has hardly anything to do with my personality.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'm afraid that I was observing Kjerag's magnificent scenery and lost track of time. Do forgive me, Holy Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I am glad to hear that you appreciate Kjerag's natural beauty.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I hope that you enjoy tonight's banquet just as much.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Indeed I will.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Ah! That's right, Harold, I have some wine here. Does your friend here drink? Come, let's have a cup or two together!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I—
The 'Trilby Asher' surreptitiously shares a hand signal with Harold.
It is a military hand signal, indicating withdrawal.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Terribly sorry, Leones.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm afraid the drink will have to wait.

steps.name: Lily
steps.text: (High-pitched braying)

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I'm back, dedushka.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Huh? Where'd he go?

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: He got pulled away by his friend in black.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: 'John'?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: ...No way.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I do hope that you managed to enjoy yourself at tonight's banquet, My Lord.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I sure was, up until you called me away.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Good, because I do not think you will enjoy this next step.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Out with it.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: There is a secret underneath the Kjeragandr statue at the heart of Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Soldiers really hate the word 'secret', Mr. 'John Smith'. Isn't this your lot's job to figure out these sort of things, rather than ours?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Unfortunately, I have no way of solving this particular issue myself.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not words I expected to hear out of a Trilby Asher.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I have run into a few obstructions.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Wait, am I hearing you right? You've failed?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Though I am unable to ascertain what exactly is down there, the very fact that I am encountering resistance is proof that I am on the right track.
The Trilby Asher takes out a stack of loose papers from the inner recesses of his coat. Within that stack are photographs, assorted documents and some handwritten notes.
Harold takes a few to look at himself, and immediately, the smile on his face freezes.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Goods loaded onto the wine transport carriages.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The true flow of the oriron supply chain.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Transport route itineraries.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: All this intelligence points towards a single fact—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Under the island at the heart of the lake lies Enciodes's secret... No, not just his, but the greatest secret of this entire nation.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...She's gone.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Allowing the daughter of a Kjerag politician to hear that was not good.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm a soldier, I only care about real battles. This is something that you intelligence agents should be handling.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She barely even knows whose daughter she is. What can she possibly do?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: If this makes her recognize what is brewing in this nation and make her cut her visit early, this is not necessarily a bad thing.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: She is, in the end, merely a citizen of Ursus. I am not one to make an enemy of that empire.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Perhaps I misjudged you during our earlier meet-ups, my good Trilby Asher.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You and me both, My Lord.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Perhaps it is a good thing that people like you and I are wary of one another.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Some real words of wisdom you got there.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: My next words might not be those words of wisdom you so adore.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You cannot go home empty-handed, My Lord.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I hope you truly understand that this is the price Enciodes must pay Her Grace.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: He has crossed a line.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Is that what you tell yourself to make it feel better?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You're far better at that sort of thing than I am.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: O Great Hero.
The banquet continues.
People gathered around the bonfire singing merry tunes and dancing, welcoming the arrival of tomorrow.
In their minds, tomorrow will certainly be a bright, jubilant, festive day, one that would compel anyone to break out into ecstatic dance and vibrant song.
'I'm probably the only one in the room who doesn't feel that way', thought Harold.
He suddenly feels a little chilly.
The last time he felt such a chill was the very first time he set foot in this land.
He felt like what he really needed was a bottle of wine. Perhaps a whole barrel.

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: Harold! I've been waiting ages for you, *hic*!

steps.name: Old Herdsman
steps.text: If you were any later, I would have finished the entire bottle myself!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hahaha, look at me! Do I look like the sort of person to miss out on fine drink?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Come! Tonight, we drink till we drop!

a.text: He's forgotten some of the finer details of what he did that night.
Perhaps he danced a merry jig from his hometown by the bonfire? Or perhaps he grabbed some unlucky fellow to sing some folk songs of Kjerag with?
Ah, that's right. He seemed to have spent a good amount of time discussing the finer points of Kjerag veterinary techniques with a guard rail.
How did he get to this point?
Alas, nobody knows.
At the very least, he remembered the way back to his bed.
However, the distance between the banquet and the barracks is no short stroll.

First, he had to follow along the lakeside path until it joined with the main street at the center of town. Along the road, he would run into many elderly folk taking a post-meal walk, and see children playing atop the ice.

From here, he could see the distant statue of Kjeragandr, and all along the road there were viewing stations set up just for gazing upon it. They were bustling places filled with people at all times. Some prayed towards Kjeragandr, while others took selfies.
There are times when two diametrically opposed ways of life will clash, but most times they will coexist in some sort of harmony. Such was the way of many things in this land.

Continuing on, he passed through the main street, which got busier by the day. He distinctly remembered noticing that some of the stores that were there when he first arrived in Kjerag had changed ownership.
In a small alley close to the center of the road, there was the latest restaurant that he had fallen in love with.
This restaurant had managed to meld together the flavors of Victoria and Kjerag together into their dishes, and suffice it to say that he was a big fan.
The restaurant was run by a young couple, the wife a Kjerag native who had learnt the culinary arts in Victoria, meeting her spouse in the process.
The two of them started a family, returning to Kjerag to set up their restaurant, hoping that they would be able to have a better life in this flourishing land.

After the alley, he had to cross a highway still under construction, then a patch of woods, before arriving at the hillside where he could look out over the whole land, where a roaring fireplace awaited him.
At the moment when he stepped over the edge of the road onto the soft soil, he became quite aware of just how much further this nation had to go to be considered 'well-developed'.
But walking through the tranquil woods immediately put a stop to that line of thinking.
Though he often jabbers away with other old men whenever they meet, lately he finds himself thinking back to the time of his youth.
The golden wheat fields rustling in the evening breeze, his younger self running about within as though he were without a care in the world—
Yes, without a single care in the world.
As he walked across the icy ground, as he found himself cloaked in snowy silence, one thought came to the forefront of his mind. He was no longer young.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Whew, you reek of booze.

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Boss, if you're going out to get roaring drunk, can't you at least bring some back for your boys?

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Boss, look here!

steps.name: Sickly Soldier
steps.text: These damned burdenbeast blind boxes! We've gotten three full sets now except for the mystery variant! This has got to be some kinda scam by Karlan Trade!

spans.text: These damned burdenbeast blind boxes! We've gotten three full sets now
for the mystery variant! This has got to be some kinda scam by Karlan Trade!

steps.text: He pulls out a remote control from the deepest recesses of his room, constantly flicking through the various slides on a projector.
Every single one has information regarding Kjerag. Possible marching routes, the locations of military bases, the distribution of sentry posts, investigations into the Tschäggättä—
Within a week of him arriving in Kjerag, all this intelligence was already neatly organized before him, and yet again and again he forced himself to stop thinking about these matters.
To the point that he has managed to memorize most of it.
He throws aside the remote control and grabs a collapsible chair close at hand, throwing himself deep into its embrace as he closes his eyes.

Rather than looking at maps and military sand tables, he much prefers listening to the subtle sounds of snow falling on branches, making them rustle and creak under its weight. It reminds him of the sound of waves of wheat—
Rustling under the moonlit breeze—

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Boss? What's the matter?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Don't mind him, he's probably just drunk off his gourd. Let's get back to what we were talking about just now.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: I heard that the Leithanians want to build a new city, mostly to get foreign trade going. Check out these preferential policies. The calculated returns for investments are unreal...
But reality never goes the way he wishes it to.
Just like how his father always yelled at him to get out of the wheat field and to continue his training at home.
Just like when his pipe stem loses a piece without him knowing.
Just like how his lost leg would never return.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: ...*sigh*
The hubbub of the barracks fades away, as his men all look towards him.
His men. His lads. His soldiers.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Everyone, change to live ammunition, then be on standby.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: At the break of dawn tomorrow, we begin our operation. Our target is—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: The statue of Kjeragandr.
His voice is somewhat hoarse.
The rustling of wheat in the wind has stopped.
